articles.title: OPENAI AND CISCO INTRODUCE SHIRUDO
articles.summary: Shirudo is an open-source runtime that lets operators deploy temporary eBPF protections on Linux while they roll out permanent patches. Teams can observe a shield's effect on live workloads before enabling it, and apply approved protections without restarting the service.

articles.title: BUILDING A CONTINUOUS SOFTWARE ENGINE THE HARD WAY
articles.summary: After an overnight coding agent kept getting stuck, its orchestrator was rebuilt to manage state, retries, and independent review in code. The new engine landed 137 verified commits across three repositories in roughly 24 hours, including benchmarks and diagnostic writeups, and still hit a scheduler deadlock.

articles.title: SPEEDING UP CODE REVIEW WITH SMALL-CHANGE
articles.summary: Imprint uses a CI check to identify pull requests eligible for a lighter review process. The check considers the size of the diff, the author's history in the affected services, and whether automated review flagged any high-priority issues.

articles.title: FAST IS A DESIGN DECISION
articles.summary: Decisions about rendering, caching, and what loads first shape how fast a site feels. On one throttled mobile test, prioritizing a small prerendered version of the homepage's lead card cut Largest Contentful Paint from about 2.5 seconds to 1.3 seconds.

articles.title: GRAPHRAG MAKES AI AGENTS 80% MORE TRUTHFUL AND 2X MORE WILLING TO ANSWER. GET STARTED WITH NEO4J
articles.summary: In a study by the National Innovation Centre for Data (NICD), graph plus vector RAG outperformed vector-only RAG on truthfulness and on answering complex questions, which means your agents can handle harder questions without making things up. Start building your own GraphRAG

articles.title: INTRODUCING CLAUDE SHIP
articles.summary: Claude Ship brings pull request review, fixes, and policy-based approvals to GitHub repositories on Claude Team and Enterprise. The new /ship command can open a PR and work through feedback and failing checks while repository rules govern what can merge.

articles.title: NUXT 4.7
articles.summary: Nuxt 4.7 lets you opt into experimental Nitro v3 on an existing Nuxt 4 app ahead of the Nuxt 5 upgrade. It also adds schema validation for runtime config, shows type and lint diagnostics in the dev overlay, and previews WebMCP support for exposing app actions to browser agents.

articles.summary: TLDR is launching a curated community for AI builders to discuss major news and launches. The best links and comments will be featured in TLDR AI. Apply here to join [14].

articles.title: GLM-5.4: TOWARD GENERALIZED CODING WITH OUR FIRST LOOP TRANSFORMER
articles.summary: Z.ai's GLM-5.4 runs the same block of 28 layers twice, giving its 750-billion-parameter model more compute per token without adding parameters for the second pass. Z.ai shows demos in CAD and video generation and reports that the model can still spend too long reasoning.

articles.title: LEGACY MODERNIZATION WITH LLMS: IS A LARGE TRANSLATION CONSISTENT WITH ITSELF?
articles.summary: An experiment used 49 Claude Code sessions to translate 600,000 lines of IBM i source into more than a million lines of Java. Deterministic generators produced the most uniform code, while independently translated programs drifted in style and duplicated helpers, with 20 implementations of a single date conversion helper.

articles.title: RUN HERMES, OPENCLAW, CLINE, AND MORE ON YOUR AMD XDNA™ 2 NPUS
articles.summary: Unsloth Desktop now supports AMD XDNA™ 2 NPUs. Its OpenAI-compatible endpoint gives 100+ agentic apps local inference

articles.title: STITCH SKILLS
articles.summary: Google's Stitch skills give coding agents reusable workflows for working with the Stitch MCP server.

articles.title: A SHORT HISTORY OF READ STREAMS IN POSTGRES
articles.summary: Postgres read streams let scans look ahead and combine adjacent disk pages into one read even when their destination buffers are scattered in memory.

articles.title: WHAT WE LEARNED OPERATING AUTH FOR 1,000+ APIS
articles.summary: After losing rotated OAuth credentials in production, Nango began persisting replacement tokens immediately and serializing refreshes per connection.
